{{Short description|German mathematician (born 1953)}}
[[File:JohannesBuchmann2016.jpg|thumb|Johannes Buchmann in 2016]]

'''Johannes Alfred Buchmann''' (born November 20, 1953, in [[Cologne]])<ref name=leo-cv>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Buchmann_Johannes_D.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae of Johannes Buchmann from the website of the Leopoldina}}</ref> is a German [[computer scientist]], [[mathematician]] and [[professor emeritus]] at the [[Department of Computer Science of TU Darmstadt|department of computer science]] of the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]].

He is known for his research in [[Computational number theory|algorithmic number theory]], [[algebra]], [[post-quantum cryptography]] and [[Computer security|IT security]]. In 1993, he received the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] together with [[Claus P. Schnorr|Claus Peter Schnorr]] for his work in algorithmic number theory and cryptography. Buchmann also developed the stateful hash-based signature scheme XMSS, the first future-proof secure and practical signature scheme with minimal security requirements, which was declared the first international standard for post-quantum [[signature scheme]]s in 2018. In addition, he further developed IT security research in Germany. His efforts led to the creation of [[Athene (research center)|ATHENE]], the largest research center for IT security in Europe. For this he received the [[Konrad Zuse Medal|Konrad Zuse Medal for Services to Computer Science]] of the [[Gesellschaft für Informatik]] (GI) in 2017.

== Life ==
Johannes Buchmann studied [[mathematics]], [[physics]], [[pedagogy]] and [[philosophy]] at the [[University of Cologne]] from 1974 to 1979 after graduating from high school in 1972 and completing his [[military service]]. After passing the first [[Staatsexamen|state examination]] for teaching at [[Gymnasium (Germany)|grammar schools]] in 1979, he taught mathematics at a Cologne secondary school from 1980 to 1983 while at the same time working as a research assistant at the university. In 1982 he did his doctorate at the university under the supervision of Hans-Joachim Stender. In 1984 he passed the second state examination. In 1985/86 he was with [[Hans Zassenhaus]] at [[Ohio State University]] on a [[scholarship]] from the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]]. From 1986 to 1988 he was research assistant of Michael Pohst at the [[Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf|University of Düsseldorf]], where he [[Habilitation|habilitated]] in 1988. Then he worked as professor of computer science at [[Saarland University]]. In 1996, he then was professor of computer science and mathematics at the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]]. He retired in 2019.<ref name=leo-cv/>

From 2001 to 2007, he was vice president for Research at the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]]. Since 2004, he has been chairman of the Board of the Competence Center for Applied Security (CAST), the largest network for [[Computer security|cyber security]] in [[List of territorial entities where German is an official language|German-speaking countries]]. From 2011 to 2013, Buchmann headed the project ''Internet Privacy - A Culture of Privacy and Trust on the Internet'' of the [[German Academy of Science and Engineering]]. He was founding director of the [[Center for Advanced Security Research Darmstadt]] (CASED) and held this position from 2008 to 2011. From 2011 to 2016, he was a member of the board of directors of the [[European Center for Security and Privacy by Design]] (EC SPRIDE). From 2016 to 2018, Buchmann was Vice Director of the [[Center for Research in Security and Privacy]] (CRISP), the largest research institute for IT security in Europe. From 2014 to 2019, he was spokesman of the [[Collaborative Research Centres|Collaborative Research Center]] CROSSING and from 2015 to 2019 spokesman of the profile area CYSEC of TU Darmstadt. He gave his farewell lecture on October 24, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tu-darmstadt.de/universitaet/aktuelles_meldungen/einzelansicht_242624.de.jsp|title=Glaubt an die Vernunft|last=Darmstadt|first=Technische Universität|date=2019-10-23|website=Technische Universität Darmstadt|language=de|access-date=2019-10-31}}</ref>

From 2017 to 2018, Johannes Buchmann trained as an MBSR ([[Mindfulness-based stress reduction|Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction]]) teacher at the Institute for Mindfulness. Since then he has been working as a certified MBSR teacher.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.johannesbuchmann.de/über-mich/|title=Johannes Buchmann - Über mich|website=www.johannesbuchmann.de|language=de|access-date=2019-10-31}}</ref>

Buchmann is married and has two sons.

== Work ==
Buchmann's achievements include scientific essays on algorithms in [[algebraic number theory]], the construction of new cryptographic methods and the use of cryptographic methods in practice. Due to his collaboration with Kálmán Győry he has the [[Erdős number]] 2.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://files.oakland.edu/users/grossman/enp/Erdos2.html|title=Erdos2, Version 2015|author=Jerry Grossman|date=2015-07-14|website=The Erdös Number Project|publisher=[[Oakland University]]|access-date=2019-06-30}}</ref> Buchmann dealt with algorithms in algebraic number theory and their application in [[cryptography]]. In 1988, he proposed with [[Hugh C. Williams]] a cryptographic system based on the [[Discrete Logarithm Problem|discrete logarithmic problem]] in the ideal class group of imaginary-square number fields (which, according to [[Carl Friedrich Gauss]], is related to the theory of binary-square forms), which triggered further developments in cryptography with number fields.<ref>[https://www-old.cdc.informatik.tu-darmstadt.de/reports/TR/TI-03-11.nfc_survey_03.pdf Buchmann, Takagi, Vollmer: ''Number field cryptography.'' Technical Report 2003] (PDF; 186&nbsp;kB)</ref>

Since 1996, Buchmann has been working intensively on the topic of [[public key infrastructure]]s, for which he published the book ''Introduction to Public Key Infrastructures'' together with Evangelos Karatsiolis and Alexander Wiesmaier in 2013.<ref>Buchmann, Johannes & Karatsiolis, Evangelos & Wiesmaier, Alexander. (2013). Introduction to Public Key Infrastructures. 10.1007/978-3-642-40657-7.</ref> Buchmann has been working on [[post-quantum cryptography]] since 2003 and published a book of the same name together with [[Daniel J. Bernstein]] and Erik Dahmen in 2009.<ref>Bernstein, Daniel J., Buchmann, Johannes, and Dahmen, Erik, ''Post-Quantum Cryptography'', 2009, Springer-Verlag, Berlin-Heidleberg. DOI: 10.1007/978-3-540-88702-7</ref> Buchmann is also the author of the textbook ''Introduction to Cryptography'', which has been translated into seven languages.<ref>Buchmann, Johannes. (2002). Introduction to Cryptography. DOI: 10.1007/978-3-642-11186-0.</ref>

In Saarbrücken, the research work of Buchmann concentrated on the theoretical cryptography and cryptanalysis of number theory-based public-key methods like RSA. During his time in Saarbrücken, Buchmann also founded the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|German Research Foundations]] first [[graduate school]] for computer science and was able to establish research in cryptography and IT security as an integral part of the university.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gfft-portal.de/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/Laudatio-auf-Prof.-Dr.-Buchmann-2016.pdf|title=Laudatio for Johannes Buchmann by José L. Encarnação}}</ref>

In 2018, the stateful hash-based signature scheme [[Hash-based cryptography|XMSS]] developed by a team of researchers under the direction of Buchmann became the first international standard for post-quantum [[Digital signature|signature schemes]]. XMSS is the first future-proof secure and practical signature scheme with minimal security requirements. The work began in 2003.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.industry-of-things.de/security-erster-standard-fuer-post-quantum-signaturen-a-732764/|title=Security: Erster Standard für Post-Quantum-Signaturen|website=www.industry-of-things.de|date=12 July 2018 |language=de|access-date=2019-10-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heise.de/security/meldung/Erster-Standard-fuer-Post-Quantum-Signaturen-4085522.html|title=Digitale Signaturen: Erster Standard für Post-Quantum-Signaturen|last=online|first=heise|website=Security|date=20 June 2018 |language=de|access-date=2019-10-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://idw-online.de/de/news697271|title=TU Darmstadt: Ein Rezept gegen die Macht der Quantencomputer|website=idw-online.de|access-date=2019-10-30}}</ref><ref>Buchmann J., Dahmen E., Hülsing A. (2011) XMSS - A Practical Forward Secure Signature Scheme Based on Minimal Security Assumptions. In: Yang BY. (eds) Post-Quantum Cryptography. PQCrypto 2011. Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol 7071. Springer, Berlin, Heidelberg</ref>

== Awards ==
* 1993 [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] (together with [[Claus P. Schnorr|Claus-Peter Schnorr]]), for his work in algorithmic number theory and cryptography
* 2002 Member of the [[Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur|Academy of Sciences and Literature Mainz]]
* 2003 Innovation Award of the State of [[Hesse]]
* 2006 Member of the [[Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities]]
* 2006 [[Honorary degree|Honorary Doctorate]] of the [[University of Debrecen]], Hungary
* 2008 Member of the [[Acatech|German Academy of Science and Engineering]]
* 2011 Member of the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|German Academy of Natural Scientists Leopoldina]]
* 2017 [[Konrad Zuse Medal|Konrad-Zuse-Medal for Services to Computer Science]] of the [[Gesellschaft für Informatik]] (GI)
